metadata.note: SCRIPT-EXACT BUILD. The nine scenes, the art direction, and the shot list follow 2026-08-28-what-is-a-concept-map.md verbatim. This is deliberately NOT a Claude-branded ai-explainer: no ClaudeComposerAsk cold open, no verdict artifact page, no YOUR TURN handoff, no title-restate outro, no channel logo bug. The Claude fidelity palette is not used. Deviations from ai-explainer frame law are logged in BUILD-LOG.md and were authorised by the human. Visuals are rendered out-of-tree (scenes/render_scenes.py) and dropped into per-beat media/ slots; the brutalist toolkit is used read-only for Kokoro narration, conform/mux, and the 9:16 derivation.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Chaitanya, and this video is about the Concept Map subsystem audit — schema, S3 layer, and why the verified output currently has zero consumers.

show.event: Ground fill, empty frame
Display title WHAT IS A CONCEPT MAP hard-snaps in on the 2nd column
Mono rule + caption MEDHAVY RESEARCH LOG / 2026-08-28 step-reveals beneath
Signal rule strikes in under the title, 6 frames, linear

beats.note: The only beat with no counterpart in the source script — it carries the requested spoken intro line. Kept to a neutral title card so no new framing is introduced: display title + mono caption + one signal rule, inside the four-value palette.

beats.narration_text: A table of contents tells you the order the author wrote things. It tells you nothing about the order a student can actually learn them. This week I went through the Concept Map subsystem — the part of the hub that tries to fix that.

show.event: Ground fill. Silence, 1 second of empty frame
Table of contents snaps in as plain mono text, left column, unstyled: CH 21 / CH 22 / CH 23
Hold 2 s
Signal line strikes through all three, left to right, 6 frames, linear
THIS IS NOT A MAP hard-snaps in, display, centered

beats.narration_text: A concept map is a knowledge graph of a textbook. Every teachable idea becomes a node. Every edge records what you need to understand first. Not what comes next in the book — what has to already be in your head for the next thing to mean anything.

show.event: Split frame, 6 cols / 6 cols, hard 4 px rule down the centre
LEFT, FIG. 01 — SEQUENCE: three chapters stacked vertically, plain mute arrows top to bottom
RIGHT, FIG. 02 — DEPENDENCY: five hard-edged node boxes, signal arrows pointing backwards into prerequisites, deliberately lopsided
Lower third step-reveals NODE = ONE TEACHABLE IDEA / EDGE = PREREQUISITE

beats.narration_text: Here's one, from the cancer textbook. Paclitaxel. Also called Taxol, which is what students will actually type. Chapter twenty-two, section one. It's a factual node — a drug name, not a mechanism. And it has one prerequisite: microtubules. Because Paclitaxel is meaningless until you know what it binds to. The name is the easy part. The edge is the part that's worth building a whole review tool for.

show.event: Single node record fills frame as a bordered data table, mono, real values from the cancer fixture
Fields reveal one row at a time, 4 frames apart, top to bottom
canonical_name highlights signal as the VO says Paclitaxel
prerequisite_nodes highlights signal as the VO reaches microtubules
Hard cut to THE EDGE IS THE POINT, display

beats.narration_text: The nodes are machine-generated. A Python pipeline reads the book, cross-references Wikipedia, and emits candidates. Machine extraction like this is roughly right and locally wrong — it invents concepts the book doesn't teach, merges two ideas into one, and picks the Wikipedia title over the term the professor actually uses. The pipeline knows this about itself. In the sample run: twenty-five nodes, and it flags six as low confidence and two as thin on source material. So the whole editor is one thing. A human gate between a machine guess and a trusted artifact.

show.event: Full-frame bar chart, brutalist: solid blocks, no axis decoration, values printed in mono directly on each bar
Bars snap in left to right on 3-frame steps: HIGH 9, MEDIUM 10, LOW 6
The LOW 6 bar fills signal. Everything else Paper
Hard cut to THIN_CONTENT: 2 in display type, signal
THE PIPELINE MARKS ITS OWN WEAK SPOTS snaps in, mono

beats.narration_text: On the way out, three fields get stripped. Wikipedia categories, confidence, and source URL — gone. That's deliberate, and it's the cleanest design decision in the subsystem. Those fields aren't facts about the book. They're scaffolding for the reviewer. Confidence is the machine telling a human where to look hardest. Once a human has looked, the number has done its job and it would be misleading to ship it downstream.

show.event: The FIG. 03 node record returns, same position, same values — now with the three reviewer-scaffolding fields present
wikipedia_categories, confidence, source_url are struck through in signal
The three struck rows fall out of frame on a 2-frame step
Remaining rows close the gap with a hard snap
SCAFFOLDING ≠ CONTENT snaps in, mono

beats.narration_text: Now the part I want on the record. I checked what reads these verified maps back. Nothing does. The write function has no counterpart. The verified type is imported by exactly two files — the thing that writes it, and the thing that defines it. Nothing in the hub ever opens the verified prefix again. The consumers are supposed to be the textbook sites, and that work is still roadmap — it's listed as a deliverable for the next-generation chassis, not as shipped code. The review pipeline is complete and correct. The consumption side is empty. That's worth knowing before anyone invests another week in the editor.

show.event: Full frame Ground
Pipeline diagram draws left to right in Paper hairlines: PIPELINE to IMPORT to REVIEW to EXPORT to S3
A final arrow extends right from S3 toward the frame edge and terminates in nothing
Empty space held for 3 full seconds. No sound
grep: 0 consumers appears mono, small, bottom right
STORED, NOT SPENT, display, signal, hard snap

beats.narration_text: That's the short version. The full video also covers the four review stages — and why export is hard-blocked while a single node is still pending — plus the dangling-edge crack the exporter never re-validates. Watch What Is a Concept Map for the whole story. The link is right below.

show.event: Hard cut to Ground
Four lines of mono, left-aligned on the 2nd column, step-revealed one per beat: CONCEPT MAP = DEPENDENCY GRAPH / REVIEW GATE = STRICT, WORKING / OUTPUT = CORRECT / CONSUMERS = 0
Everything cuts to black except the last line
CONSUMERS 0 held in signal for 2 s
Hard cut to black
